items.text: Real self-care pages: a weekly check-in (mood, energy, sleep, one kind thing a day, gentle habits), a self-care menu of ideas by time, an energy map, a hard day plan, monthly mood colors and a year in moods.
Journal space: a prompt page for every week with lined space, three small good things and a kind word to myself, a monthly reflection and three notes pages.
One PDF that works in Goodnotes (named first), Notability, Samsung Notes, Xodo and Noteshelf on iPad, Android and Windows tablets.
Fully hyperlinked: Contents, month tabs on every page, a top bar, previous and next arrows, and a trail back on every page.
A finished, calm look with real typography; design is the biggest praise driver.
Instructions printed inside the file (Start here and Setup check), not only in a separate guide.

complaint:c_download: Ships as one PDF, not a zip and not a guide that points somewhere else (a 1-star buyer only found the guide). Listing copy and the apps photo give the download in 3 steps: buy, download from Etsy in a web browser (the Etsy app cannot download digital files), open the PDF in a note app. Start here repeats them.

complaint:c_not_useful: It has the weekly plan a 1-star buyer missed: a week page with a row for every day, plus a journal page for the same week. Photos show the pages close up so buyers can judge them, and the listing lists every page type with its count.

complaint:c_value: Not a single worksheet: 52 week pages and 52 prompt pages, each with a different printed prompt, plus 13 month pages, a journal index, a year in moods, a self-care menu, an energy map and a hard day plan, all linked. Every writing row is at least 7 mm tall (US college-ruled spacing). The listing gives exact counts from the built file.

complaint:c_hard: One page to learn: the week page. It holds the whole week (a row per day for mood, energy, sleep and one kind thing, and 5 gentle habits) and opens that week's journal and the self-care menu with buttons. Start here step 3 walks through exactly this. Nothing to build yourself: every page is laid out and filled with labels.

complaint:c_quality: Every printed word, including all 52 prompts, is spell-checked before publishing, and the build checks 0 broken links, no unreachable pages and no overflowing text. Vector text stays crisp at any zoom.

complaint:c_device: Plain PDF links every major note app follows, landscape pages at the tablet's own shape. The listing has a Works with and Not for box (not for phones, not Canva, not a fillable form) and says how to type with the text tool. Setup check proves the links on the buyer's own device.
complaint:c_misleading: Every listing photo is the built file, captioned with the page name, and the description counts each page type from the built file (style rule r003): no padded page counts.

complaint:c_basic: Content, not only boxes: 52 different printed prompts, a self-care menu with 20 ideas sorted by how much time you have, a hard day plan with the smallest steps already written, and mood colors that build into a year in moods.
complaint:c_missing: Weekly plans are included (the 1-star complaint), and no extras are promised that could go missing: no stickers, no bonus files. Contents shows every section on one screen.

complaint:c_overwhelm: Small on purpose: about 130 pages, one week page and one journal page a week, no daily pages to fall behind on. Start here gives 4 steps and says where to begin. The top bar never shows more than 7 buttons.

complaint:c_setup: The cover's Open planner button lands on Start here: 4 numbered steps, steps 2 to 4 with Go there buttons. Setup check is next: buttons that jump and come back, with a fix list if they do not. There is nothing to edit or set up before planning.

complaint:c_nav: A calm layout and few page types. Every page has month tabs, a top bar (Home, Weeks, Journal, Menu, Energy, Hard day, Moods), arrows and a trail at the top right that works as a back button; a 52-week overview opens any week in one tap, and each week's journal page sits right after it in the file.

complaint:c_support: The answers live in the file and the listing: the Setup check fix list, Start here and a listing FAQ (Etsy app download, which app, links not tapping, how to type). Reply speed is shop-level, and the file promises no reply times (style rule r007).

complaint:c_edit: Nothing to edit before use. Blank habit rows, a blank menu row in every group and write-in energy lists make it the buyer's own. Start here and the listing say how to type with the app's text tool, and that it is not a fillable form.

A journal prompt for every week: 52 journal pages, each with its own printed prompt, linked from its week page and back, with three small good things and a kind word to myself. A journal index lists all 52 prompts, one tap each; the top bar's Journal button opens it.

Self-care menu and hard day plan: A self-care menu of ideas sorted by time (5 minutes, 15 minutes, an hour, a slow day) with blank rows to add your own, an energy map (what drains me, what fills me back up, boundaries) and a hard day plan with the smallest steps already written. Every week page has a button to the menu.
Small on purpose: One week page and one journal page a week, 12 month pages and a handful of tools: about 130 linked pages, not 1,500. Nothing piles up when you skip a few days.
Five-minute start and setup check: Start here (4 steps; steps 2 to 4 have Go there buttons) and Setup check (buttons that jump and return, with a fix list) open from the cover.

Start any week, keep it every year: Undated weeks and months: write the dates the day you start. No year to run out, so the same file works next year too. A 13th undated month page (Month 13) covers a run that starts mid-month, and Year in moods has a Year to ____ line.

Quiet dusk, not rainbow ADHD and not dark mode. Warm cream paper (#FCF8F3, soft in a dark room) with deep plum ink at about 12:1 contrast; muted text stays above 5:1. Plum buttons, peach and lavender month tabs, a honey ring on the cover. Two fonts only: Cormorant Garamond for headings and, in italic, for labels; Nunito for body text, with bold for buttons and days. No letter-spaced capitals, no clip-art flowers or cartoon girls. Landscape, so it reads differently from our portrait planners.
